raw_response:
I am old now, and I do this the same way I have learned on my own land. I cannot gamble with all 8 mu. The wheat-maize land is still my main land because that is the steadiest money here. If wheat is decent, maize after it usually gives me something too. Cotton I will keep on a smaller piece because it takes more picking, but it spreads the risk. Mungbean I keep on a little piece because it does not cost much, it can stand some dry weather, and we can also keep some at home. I will not push the inputs too hard. Fertilizer and water both cost money, and some people in the family work outside, so I cannot count on everybody being free exactly when I need them. I will do what worked in past years: put enough fertilizer so the crop does not go hungry, irrigate when the crop really needs it, and not leave myself with no cash in hand.
